questions.text: Explain any three reasons for the nationalist upsurge in the 19th century Europe.
questions.answer:
i. The absolute rulers oppressed the people.
ii. Well-known philosophers and leaders spread liberal ideas and visions.
iii. The French Revolution inspired the people to fight for freedom.
iv. The slogan 'Liberty, Equality and Fraternity' became the clarion call for the common people of Europe.
v. The French army and its soldiers began to carry the ideas of nationalism abroad with the outbreak of revolutionary wars.

or.text: Who were the architects of the unification of Germany?
or.answer: The Prussian Chancellor Bismarck and the Prussian King William-I were the chief architects of the unification of Germany.

questions.text: Why did the Muslim Ulama in India want to introduce religious reforms in Islam? Give any three reasons.
questions.answer:
i. In North India, the decline of the Muslim dynasties deeply disturbed the ulama and caused anxiety in them.
ii. They started considering themselves a minority religion and felt the need for reforms.
iii. They feared that colonial rulers would encourage conversion and change Muslim personal laws; they were not ready to give in.
iv. To counter this, they used cheap lithographic presses to publish Persian and Urdu translations of holy scriptures and printed religious newspapers and tracts.
v. The Deoband Seminary, founded in 1867, published thousands of fatwas telling Muslim readers how to conduct themselves in everyday life and explaining the meanings of Islamic doctrines.

or.text: In which three ways did the printed books at first closely resembled the written manuscripts?
or.answer:
i. Both printed books and manuscripts looked similar because metal letters imitated the ornamental handwritten style.
ii. Like written manuscripts, the borders of printed books were illuminated by hand with foliage and patterns painted.
iii. In both, space for decoration was kept blank so that the buyer could choose the designs.

questions.text: "Culture played an important role in creating the idea of the nation in 19th century Europe." Evaluate the statement in the context of romanticism.
questions.answer: In 19th-century Europe, culture played a crucial role in shaping the idea of the nation, especially through Romanticism, a movement that encouraged nationalist feelings. Romantic artists and poets rejected the excessive focus on reason and science, highlighting emotions, intuition and the spiritual bond that united people. They aimed to create a sense of shared cultural heritage as the foundation of nationhood. Thinkers like Johann Gottfried Herder argued that true German culture lived among common people, expressed in folk songs, folk tales and dances. Collecting and preserving these traditions became central to nation-building. The Grimm brothers viewed such folklore as the pure spirit of Germany. In Poland, the use of the Polish language in churches resisted Russian control, while artists like Karol Kurpinski turned folk music and dances into strong nationalist symbols.

or.text: How did nationalism aligned with imperialism become the cause of the First World War? Explain.
or.answer: Towards the last quarter of the nineteenth century, nationalism could not retain its idealistic liberal-democratic sentiment of the first half of the century but became a narrow belief with inadequate ends. Nationalist groups became increasingly intolerant, which leads to war. Major European powers manipulated the nationalist aspirations to further their own imperialist aims. Nationalism, aligned with imperialism, led Europe to disaster in 1914. The anti-imperial movements that developed everywhere were nationalist, in that they all struggled to form independent nation-states, inspired by a sense of collective national unity forged in confrontation with imperialism. As the different Slavic nationalities struggled to define their identity and independence, the Balkan area became an area of intense conflict. The Balkan states were fiercely jealous of each other and each hoped to gain more territory at the expense of the others. Matters were further complicated because the Balkans also became the scene of big power rivalry over trade and colonies as well as naval and military might. Each power - Russia, Germany, England, Austria-Hungary - was keen on countering the hold of other powers over the Balkans and extending its own control over the area. This led to a series of wars in the region and finally the First World War.

questions.text:
Read the following source and answer the questions that follow:
The Independence Day Pledge, 26 January 1930
"We believe that it is the inalienable right of the Indian people, as of any other people, to have freedom and to enjoy the fruits of their toil and have the necessities of life, so that they may have full opportunities of growth. We also believe that if any government deprives people of these rights and oppresses them, the people have a further right to alter it or abolish it. The British Government in India has not only deprived the Indian people of their freedom but based itself on the exploitation of the masses, and has ruined India economically, politically, culturally and spiritually. We believe, therefore, that India must sever the British connection and attain Purna Swaraj or Complete Independence."

ii. The British Government in India deprived the Indian people of their freedom.
iii. They exploited the masses. (any two)

questions.text:
Define the following terms:
i. Current fallow land
ii. Other than current fallow
iii. Culturable waste land
questions.answer:
i. Current fallow land: land left uncultivated for one or less than one agricultural year.
ii. Other than current fallow land: land left uncultivated for the past 1 to 5 agricultural years.
iii. Culturable waste land: land left uncultivated for more than 5 agricultural years; it was used in the past but has been abandoned for some reason.

questions.text: "Formation of coal is a long drawn process spread over various periods." Elaborate the statement with examples in the Indian context.
questions.answer: Coal is a naturally occurring black material, a mixture of carbon and compounds of carbon containing hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen and sulphur. Its formation is called fossilation; it is formed by the compression of plant material over millions of years. Indian coal was mainly formed during two geological ages, the Gondwana and the Tertiary ages. The Gondwana coal deposits (metallurgical coal), more than 200 million years old, are located in the Damodar valley (West Bengal-Jharkhand), where Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro are important coalfields. It is also found in the Godavari, Mahanadi, Son and Wardha valleys. The Tertiary age deposits, only about 55 million years old, are mostly found in North-Eastern India in Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland. Thus the formation of coal is a long drawn process spread over various periods.

or.text: Explain the measures taken by 'National Thermal Power Corporation' to prevent environmental degradation.
or.answer: The corporation follows a proactive approach to preserving the natural environment and conserving resources such as water, oil, gas and fuels wherever it establishes power plants. This is achieved through optimum use of equipment, adoption of the latest technologies and continuous upgrading of existing systems to enhance efficiency. Waste generation is minimised by maximising the utilisation of ash. It develops extensive green belts to maintain ecological balance and promotes afforestation through special-purpose vehicles. To reduce pollution it implements ash pond management, ash water recycling systems and liquid waste management. Ecological monitoring and regular environmental reviews are carried out across all power stations, and an online database system is maintained to track environmental performance.

questions.text:

However, the internal demand has been on the increase due to the Government policy of mandatory use of jute packaging. To stimulate demand, the products need to be diversified. In 2005, National Jute Policy was formulated with the objective of increasing productivity, improving quality, ensuring good prices to the jute farmers and enhancing the yield per hectare. The main markets are U.S.A., Canada, Russia, United Arab Republic, U.K. and Australia. The growing global concern for environment friendly, biodegradable materials, has once again opened the opportunity for jute products.

subparts.text: What was the main objective of National Jute Policy formulated in 2005?
subparts.answer: To increase productivity, improve quality, ensure good prices to the farmers and enhance the yield per hectare.

subparts.text: How has jute industry once again opened the new opportunities for its products?
subparts.answer: a. Biodegradable materials have once again opened the opportunity for jute products. b. The global concern for environment-friendly products is increasing day by day. c. Synthetic substitutes are being avoided.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements will be considered as a factor that contributes to strengthening federalism and democracy in our country?
Statement i: Not a single national party is able to secure on its own a majority in the general elections.
Statement ii: Every party in the country registers with the Election Commission.
Statement iii: The Election Commission classifies major parties as 'State parties'.
Statement iv: State parties get an opportunity to be a part of one or the other national-level coalition government.
options: Statement i, ii and iii are right.
Statement i and ii are right.
questions.answer: (c) Only statement iv is right. No national party was able to secure a majority in the Lok Sabha on its own until 2014, so national parties formed alliances with State parties. Since 1996 nearly every State party has had an opportunity to be part of a national-level coalition government, strengthening federalism and democracy.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): Sex-selective abortion led to the decline of the sex ratio in India.
Reason (R): Desire for a male child makes Indian families abort girls.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.answer: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. Indian parents who want a son seek ways to abort a girl child; sex-selective abortion is immoral and legally banned in India.

questions.text: How can power be shared among governments at different levels? Explain.
questions.answer: Vertical division of power means sharing of power among governments at different levels. In India there are three levels of government: i. for the entire country - Central (Union) Government; ii. at the provincial level - State Governments; iii. at the local level (rural and urban) - local self-governments like panchayats and municipal councils. Under this division involving higher and lower levels of government, the lower organs work under the higher organs.

questions.text: Mention the two conditions that democracy must fulfil in order to achieve a harmonious social life.
questions.answer:
i. Democracy is not just rule by majority opinion; the majority and minority must always work together so that governments function to represent the general view.
ii. The rule by the majority should not become rule by the majority community in terms of religion, race, linguistic group, etc.

questions.text: Why is it said that democracies are not free from evils? Explain.
questions.answer:
A. Most democracies fall short of elections that provide a fair chance to everyone and of subjecting every decision to public debate.
B. Democratic governments do not have a very good record in sharing information with citizens.
C. Democracies often frustrate the needs of the people and often ignore the demands of a majority of the population.

questions.text: Describe the role of opposition party in democracy.
questions.answer:
i. Scrutiny and accountability: the opposition calls attention to the government's weaknesses and holds it responsible for its actions and policies.
ii. Alternative viewpoints: it offers different ideas and solutions, giving voters a choice and fostering healthy debate.
iii. Power in waiting: it acts as a government-in-waiting, ready to take power if it wins the next election, which keeps the ruling party on its toes.
iv. Protecting minority interests: it represents the voices and interests of minority groups so their concerns are not overlooked.
v. Checks and balances: through parliamentary mechanisms it acts as a vital check on the ruling party's power.

or.text: State the various functions political parties perform in a democracy.
or.answer:
A. Parties contest elections; in most democracies elections are fought mainly among candidates put up by parties, who select candidates in different ways.
B. Parties put forward different policies and programmes and voters choose from them; a government is expected to base its policies on the line taken by the ruling party.
C. Parties play a decisive role in making laws; laws are debated and passed in the legislature, most of whose members belong to political parties.
D. Parties form and run governments; big policy decisions are taken by the political executive that comes from the parties.
E. Parties that lose elections play the role of opposition, voicing different views and criticising the government for failures or wrong policies.
F. They shape public opinion by raising and highlighting issues.
G. They provide people a way to access government machinery and welfare schemes.

questions.text:
Read the following source and answer the questions that follow:
Local Self Government
The local government structure goes right up to the district level. A few gram panchayats are grouped together to form what is usually called a panchayat samiti or block or mandal. The members of this representative body are elected by all the panchayat members in that area. All the panchayat samitis or mandals in a district together constitute the zilla (district) parishad. Most members of the zilla parishad are elected. Members of the Lok Sabha and MLAs of that district and some other officials of other district level bodies are also its members. Zilla parishad chairperson is the political head of the zilla parishad.
Similarly, local government bodies exist for urban areas as well. Municipalities are set up in towns. Big cities are constituted into municipal corporations. Both municipalities and municipal corporations are controlled by elected bodies consisting of people's representatives. Municipal chairperson is the political head of the municipality. In a municipal corporation, such an officer is called the mayor.
This new system of local government is the largest experiment in democracy conducted anywhere in the world.

subparts.text: Explain the relationship between gram panchayats and panchayat samitis.
subparts.answer: A few gram panchayats are grouped to form a panchayat samiti; the Panchayat Samiti acts as a link between the Zila Parishad and the Gram Panchayat.

subparts.text: How is the structure of municipal corporation different from municipality?
subparts.answer: A Municipal Corporation is an urban local self-government body that administers a big city (its political head is the mayor), whereas a Municipality administers a town (its political head is the municipal chairperson).

subparts.text: How does the local government structure promote democracy? Examine.
subparts.answer: i. It promotes grass-root level democracy. ii. It deepens democracy. iii. It increases women's participation. iv. It ensures participation of people in decision making.

questions.text: Starting around 1991, the Indian government made far-reaching changes in policy to encourage ________ competition.
questions.answer: (b) Global. The government decided that the time had come for Indian producers to compete with producers around the globe.

questions.text: Only income is not the proper indicator of the development of the country. Which of the following is not correct in the context of the above statement?
options: Money helps us buy only material goods and services
Money cannot ensure a pollution-free environment for individuals
Some people earn more than others do
Money does not ensure respect and dignity for individuals
questions.answer: (c) Some people earn more than others do. Income criteria consider only the economic aspect and ignore the social aspect of life; money cannot buy a pollution-free environment, unadulterated medicines, or protection from infectious diseases unless the whole community takes preventive steps.

A farmer produces one ton of wheat and sells it for 100 to a flour mill. As far as the farmer is concerned, the sale of wheat is a final sale for him. But the purchase of wheat by the flour mill is an intermediate good. He converts the wheat into flour and sells it to a baker for 150. The baker sells the bread to the shopkeeper for 200, and the shopkeeper to the consumer for 250. Classify the good (bread) that is sold by the baker to the shopkeeper.
questions.answer: (b) Final Goods. Final goods are ready for use/consumption and need no further value addition, whereas intermediate goods are used for resale or further production. For the baker, flour is an intermediate good; the bread is sold on to the consumer, so it is a final good.

questions.text: How use of containers has helped much greater volumes of goods being transported by airlines?
questions.answer: Goods are placed in containers that can be loaded intact into planes. Containers have led to a huge reduction in port handling costs and increased the speed with which exports can reach markets. Similarly, the cost of air transport has fallen. This has enabled much greater volumes of goods to be transported by airlines, the fastest means of transportation.

questions.text: "Poor households still depend on informal sources of credit". Support the statement with examples.
questions.answer:
i. In rural areas, banks are not present everywhere.
ii. Even where banks are present, getting a bank loan is much more complicated than taking a loan from informal sources.
iii. Proper documentation and collateral are required by banks.
iv. Absence of collateral is a major reason that prevents the poor from getting bank loans.
v. Informal lenders such as moneylenders know the borrowers personally and are willing to give a loan without collateral.

questions.text: Although average incomes are useful for comparing countries, they also hide disparities? Explain the meaning of this statement.
questions.answer:
Average or per capita incomes are useful for comparing the economic conditions of two countries but they hide disparities and inequalities and do not give a true picture of an economy:
i. They do not tell how equally or evenly income is distributed among different sections of society.
ii. They do not give information about human development indicators such as literacy rate, infant mortality rate, etc.
iii. Averages give no idea about non-materialistic goods and services, i.e. those that cannot be measured in monetary terms.

questions.text: Highlight any five features of Private Sector.
questions.answer:
i. Ownership of assets and delivery of services is in the hands of individuals, groups of individuals or companies; private entrepreneurs own, control and manage the business.
ii. Activities are guided by the motive to earn more profits.
iii. Jobs are not secure; the private sector has a competitive work culture and employee performance is very important for career growth and compensation.
iv. Private sector does not provide basic facilities at reasonable rates.
v. They may not continue their production or business unless the government encourages and supports them.

or.text: "Agriculture and industries complement each other." Justify the statement.
or.answer: Agriculture and industries are closely linked and support each other's growth; neither can progress effectively in isolation. Agro-based industries such as food processing, textile, sugar and dairy have significantly boosted agricultural productivity by creating a steady demand for farm produce. Industries depend heavily on agriculture for raw materials like cotton, jute, sugarcane and oilseeds. Industries strengthen agriculture by supplying inputs such as fertilizers, pesticides, insecticides, irrigation pumps, tractors, harvesters, PVC pipes and other modern tools, making farming more efficient, scientific and productive and reducing manual labour. In the age of globalisation, industries must remain competitive and technologically advanced; when they become more efficient they produce better-quality agricultural inputs at affordable prices, further increasing agricultural productivity. Thus agriculture and industry move hand in hand and complement each other.
